core_obligations: Give the coupling argument for Glauber dynamics, following the cited sketch, by bounding the probability that a coordinate remains out of equilibrium (source lines 926-955).
Transfer the bound to the systematic scan by comparing the two chains step by step, which is where the constant c times n appears (source lines 956-990).
Read off the conclusion that the general upper bound is tight up to the logarithmic factor in the smallest stationary probability (source line 990).

proof_roadmap.step: Coupling bound for Glauber dynamics on the complete graph.
Comparison with the systematic scan and the tightness conclusion.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the theorem at source lines 917-923, whose heading attributes it to a cited paper and whose proof is written out in this manuscript: for the hardcore model on the complete graph with fugacity one and any scan order, the mixing time of the systematic scan is at least a constant times n times the mixing time of Glauber dynamics, so that the general upper bound is tight up to the logarithm of the inverse smallest stationary probability. The proof (source lines 925-990) does not merely quote the source: it sets up a coupling for Glauber dynamics, bounds the probability that a coordinate stays out of equilibrium, and then compares the two chains step by step to produce the linear factor. The statement records the comparison and neither the coupling nor the step-by-step comparison.
